title: Fundamentals of Generative AI - Week 10 Assignment 10
subject: Fundamentals of Generative AI

questions.question: 1. What is the primary advantage of the Transformer architecture over RNNs and LSTMs?
options: It processes tokens sequentially, reducing memory usage.
It requires fewer parameters than RNNs.
It eliminates the need for positional information.
It uses self-attention to process all tokens in parallel, enabling efficient learning of long-range dependencies.
questions.correctAnswer: It uses self-attention to process all tokens in parallel, enabling efficient learning of long-range dependencies.
questions.explanation: Self-attention enables parallel sequence processing and connects any two tokens in O(1) path length regardless of distance.

questions.question: 2. Why are positional encodings added to the input embeddings in a Transformer?
options: To provide information about the order of tokens since self-attention itself is order-independent.
To increase the vocabulary size.
To reduce the number of model parameters.
To replace token embeddings.
questions.correctAnswer: To provide information about the order of tokens since self-attention itself is order-independent.
questions.explanation: Self-attention is permutation-equivariant; positional encodings provide essential word order and structural positioning.

questions.question: 3. Which statement correctly distinguishes encoder self-attention from decoder masked self-attention?
options: Encoder self-attention attends only to previoustokens.
Decoder masked self-attention prevents each token from attending to future tokens during training.
Both mechanisms use identical attention masks.
Encoder self-attention ignores positional encodings.
questions.correctAnswer: Decoder masked self-attention prevents each token from attending to future tokens during training.
questions.explanation: Causal masking prevents the decoder from attending to future tokens, preserving the autoregressive property during training.

questions.question: 4. BERT is primarily trained using which learning objective?
options: Next-word prediction only.
Masked Language Modeling (MLM) and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP).
Image classification.
Reinforcement learning.
questions.correctAnswer: Masked Language Modeling (MLM) and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP).
questions.explanation: BERT is pretrained on Masked Language Modeling (MLM) and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP).

questions.question: 5. Why is BERT considered a bidirectional language model?
options: It predicts text from right to left only.
It processes the input sequence using context from both the left and right of each token.
It uses two separate encoders.
It translates text in both directions.
questions.correctAnswer: It processes the input sequence using context from both the left and right of each token.
questions.explanation: BERT uses unmasked self-attention across the entire sequence to condition representations on both left and right contexts.

questions.question: 6. GPT differs from BERT because GPT:
options: Uses only the encoder stack of the Transformer.
Uses only the decoder stack with masked self-attention for autoregressive text generation.
Is trained only on labeled datasets.
Does not use self-attention.
questions.correctAnswer: Uses only the decoder stack with masked self-attention for autoregressive text generation.
questions.explanation: GPT is an autoregressive decoder-only Transformer model designed for left-to-right generation.

questions.question: 7. Which application is more suitable for GPT than BERT?
options: Sentiment classification
Named Entity Recognition (NER)
Automatic text generation and conversational AI
Masked word prediction
questions.correctAnswer: Automatic text generation and conversational AI
questions.explanation: Autoregressive generation models like GPT excel at open-ended text completion and dialogue generation.

questions.question: 8. In prompt engineering, what is the primary purpose of providing few-shot examples?
options: To guide the model toward the desired response format or reasoning pattern without updating its parameters.
To retrain the language model.
To reduce the vocabulary size.
To increase the model's training accuracy.
questions.correctAnswer: To guide the model toward the desired response format or reasoning pattern without updating its parameters.
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting provides in-context demonstrations that guide formatting and reasoning behavior without weight optimization.

questions.question: 9. Which of the following prompts is an example of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting?
options: Translate the following sentence into French.
Classify this review as positive or negative.
Solve the problem step by step before giving the final answer.
Summarize the following paragraph in one sentence.
questions.correctAnswer: Solve the problem step by step before giving the final answer.
questions.explanation: 'Let's think step by step' is canonical Chain-of-Thought prompting, directing the model to output intermediate reasoning steps.

questions.question: 10. Which statement correctly compares BERT and GPT?
options: BERT uses an encoder-only architecture for bidirectional language understanding, whereas GPT uses a decoder-only architecture for autoregressive text generation.
BERT and GPT both use encoder-only architectures but differ only in the size of their training datasets.
GPT is bidirectional and predicts masked tokens, whereas BERT predicts the next word using causal attention.
Both BERT and GPT require paired input-output datasets during pretraining.
questions.correctAnswer: BERT uses an encoder-only architecture for bidirectional language understanding, whereas GPT uses a decoder-only architecture for autoregressive text generation.
questions.explanation: BERT is an encoder-only bidirectional understanding architecture, while GPT is a decoder-only autoregressive causal generation architecture.
